## Summary

Skill proposal: **/fix-one-thing** — "Read CODING_STANDARDS.md. Find a violation in the codebase, and fix it. Make the PR small and easy to review, with a small blast radius." Run it whenever there's a spare moment, or once an hour on a schedule.

## Why it matters

- **This is the missing execution half of the standards-accretion loop.** [[2026-09-26-pocock-coding-standards-accretion]] covers where standards come from (observed failures, accreting into CODING_STANDARDS.md); this skill is what *spends* them: a cron-able agent that converts accreted rules into a steady drip of tiny reviewable PRs. Accrete → enforce → repeat.
- **Porting to our own scaffolding is trivial in shape:** our equivalent of CODING_STANDARDS.md already exists in agglomerated form (skills Pitfalls sections, AGENTS.md conventions). A /fix-one-thing-style pass would target our own repos' drift — but the trading company's repos are out of scope here; the natural first target is this vault + personal tooling.
- **"Once an hour on a schedule" is the interesting scaling lever**: continuous background repair instead of cleanup binges — the same cadence argument as our heartbeat/cron posture.
- **Skepticism gates:** idea tweet, not a shipped skill — mechanics (violation-finding reliability, PR volume vs review capacity) unproven; an hourly PR drip can outpace review, recreating the slop problem it solves.
